note: Only what needs a person. Done, decided and unrelated meeting follow-ups were removed on Oct 21, 2026 (git history has the old list).

items.title: Where the toolkits live on bigleap.com
items.detail: The site is public at bigl3ap.github.io/bigleap-diy-toolkits. Decide where it's linked from on bigleap.com and whether it gets its own address (e.g. tools.bigleap.com, one DNS record).
items.rec: Link it from Resources › Tools now; add the subdomain when it's promoted.

items.title: Consent model before turning on analytics
items.detail: Every page already sends diy_* events, but no tags load: the Tag Manager and HubSpot IDs are blank. Decide how consent works before adding them.
items.rec: Turn on GTM with consent mode, sending event names only. Get explicit opt-in before any follow-up email or 'email me my plan'.

items.title: Should RevOps 1–6 fill in from the Business Profile?
items.detail: They're the live set and the only toolkits that don't. Visitors who built a profile re-answer the same questions there.
items.rec: Yes, read-only, built and tested on a branch first. RevOps 7 shows the pattern.

items.title: Agency Brands routing for toolkit leads
items.detail: The journey map describes routing by what the client is buying (Big Leap, Set Fire, LeadGenix, STS). Nothing routes automatically today.
items.rec: Approve the rules first; keep routing manual until then.

items.title: Who decides 'load-bearing', and can DIY work reduce scope?
items.detail: The foundations starter lets visitors mark work as usable or not. The SOP lists a written standard and the discovery fee as open.
items.rec: Write a one-page standard. No credits or prices on the site until it exists.

items.title: Where Sweet Takes guest requests should go
items.detail: Coby's idea is live on PR 01, PR 02 and the brand starter. 'Ask about being a guest' goes to the contact page, tagged utm_medium=sweet-takes-guest.
items.rec: Send it to a short guest form or your inbox, and confirm the wording 'asking doesn't book a spot'.

items.title: Sign off the Strategy starters and the roadmap
items.detail: They adapt your Situation Audit, Gap Audit, brand ideology and Recommend Delight for a self-serve audience, and they're live. Check: do the market, health and motion rules match the Situation Audit? Do usable / not load-bearing / missing / unknown match the Gap Audit? Is starter 3 fine as a light version of brand ideology? Starters 3 and 4 show 'Coby review' until you sign off. Also confirm the three-motions wording on the journey map.

items.title: Review Paid Media 1–4
items.detail: Confirm or correct: $1,000/mo ready for one campaign, $1,500 for a second, 70–85% on the main one. Google Ads only in v1? GA4 key events or Ads tags, and which CRM stages go back to Ads? The 'talk to Scott first' verticals (car dealers, legal, healthcare, finance, housing). Click every menu path in Paid 3 and RevOps 7 once.

items.title: Review SEO 1–2
items.detail: Confirm you own these. Is 'allow search bots; blocking AI training bots is the client's choice' Big Leap's position? Which AI-search checks stay? Is a third toolkit (content and keywords) wanted, or expert-only?

items.title: Review Digital PR 1–2
items.detail: Is 24–48 hours the right reply bar for journalists? Are 50/150-word bios right? Do paid podcast-guest lists belong in a v2? Is the line between DIY and proprietary in the right place? Share your PR toolkit doc if you'd like it worked in.

items.title: Review Email Marketing 1–3
items.detail: Which platforms lead (Mailchimp, Klaviyo, HubSpot, Constant Contact)? Are the Email 3 benchmark ranges yours (e.g. spam complaints under 0.1%)? Should legal check the email-law table in Email 1? Is a 4th toolkit on sign-up forms wanted?

items.title: Review RevOps 1–7
items.detail: Confirm the hosted RevOps 5 is the v2 build. Walk RevOps 7's menu paths with Scott.

items.title: Send your scheduler link for the 'Talk to …' button
items.detail: Every 'Talk to' button goes to bigleap.com/contact-us with UTMs. Send Dallas a booking link and it gets swapped in.

items.title: Send the Masterclass signup URL
items.detail: From the Oct 13 sync: toolkits should link to the Masterclass signup. The page address isn't on record yet.

items.title: Test on a real iPhone (Safari) and in Firefox
items.detail: Every page passes in Chromium at desktop and phone widths, light and dark. Real Safari and Firefox haven't been tried.

items.title: Save the HubSpot report for toolkit-sourced pipeline
items.detail: Contacts and deals with original source campaign diy-toolkits, by toolkit and lifecycle stage. Counts toward the $400K marketing-sourced MRR goal. Works once tags are on.

items.title: Content Go/No-Go toolkit
items.detail: Content is the one service without a toolkit. Send the go/no-go framework and it can be built in the same style.

items.owner: Dallas Olsen, Erica Pounder, Scott Smoot
items.title: Follow-up emails, sales alerts and retargeting
items.detail: The plan-delivery sequence, high-intent alert, retargeting audiences and MQL rule on the journey map all wait on the consent decision.

items.title: Set real KPI targets
items.detail: The journey map's targets are examples. Set real ones after 60 days of data.

items.detail: One shared Business Profile box and one place for 'Where it gets complex' on every toolkit.
